title: How to run a reading session for children · AquaTerra
description: How AquaTerra runs storytelling, speaking and English sessions for children: one skill, a host, a small team and a write-up. {count} drives since {firstYear}.
lede: Since {firstYear}, AquaTerra has written up {count} drives under reading, storytelling and English, most of them small sessions with a few volunteers and a room of children. Each one starts from a single skill, a clear prompt and a story to tell.

sections.heading: pick one skill for the session
body: Choose one skill and build the session around it. The sessions on this page covered storytelling and story making, public speaking, English grammar and money basics. Titles such as Tale Time, Speak Skillfully and Budget Basics name the skill, so the children know what the session is about.

Use a prompt and a game for the middle of the session. Speak Smart was taught through games, Tale Time built its stories from guided prompts, and Spine and Story, a Halloween session, had children create and share their own tales. A prompt gives everyone the same place to start.

sections.heading: set up with the host
body: Most sessions ran at a place where children already come together. Pather Sathi and Disha Foundation have hosted the most sessions on this page, with Ek Tara, Newlight Ngo, AIM Foundation and School On Wheels hosting several more. Call the host a few days before, agree the room, and ask what the children are already working on, so the session fits.

Keep the group small. Sessions on this page usually had two to five volunteers, which let each volunteer sit with a few children. The Teaching English Workshop at Ektara Foundation in April 2026 had five volunteers for fifteen children, who learned conjunctions and verbs.

sections.heading: on the day
body: Open with something the children already know, then move to the skill. The December 2025 session at Pather Sathi started with Christmas carols, with the children singing alongside the volunteers, and ended with cake and classic festive stories. That order is worth borrowing: warm up, practise the skill, and finish on a story.

Let the children speak, and make it a game when you can. PowerSpeak taught public speaking through storytelling and art. Speech Ready introduced children to talking in front of an audience. Telling Tales set out to turn shy voices into storytellers.
Keep the English close to play. The English sessions covered word play and grammar, and Nature x English took the lessons outdoors in 2023, with poems, leaves and stories.

sections.heading: let a good theme come back
body: A theme can run as a short series. Nature x English ran as four sessions, from 16 June to 7 July 2023, and Speak to Shine ran as two, on 11 May and 22 June 2023. A series also gives a team a theme it already knows how to run.
Write each session up with the children's skill, the place and the team. The write-ups are public on the site, so a new team can see what a reading session looked like before planning its own.

sections.heading: the notebook drives beside the sessions
body: Not every drive on this page is a session. [Wear and Write](/impact/wear-and-write), our clothes and notebook collection, has run in many rounds since April 2024, and the collected notebooks go to children who need them. Toy and Thread collected clothes and toys in March 2025. These are a different kind of drive from the lessons, so plan them as their own job.

sections.heading: run one with a team
body: Members of AquaTerra run these sessions, and students aged 14 to 19 can join. Sign in with Google to start, and your membership is approved before you take part in a drive. If you are a teacher or a school, the For teachers and educators page shows the formats, and the [collaborations page](/collaborations) is where to begin.

learnings: One skill per session gives children a clear reason to speak, read or write, and the titles say it: Tale Time, Speak Skillfully, Budget Basics.
A prompt or a game can do the warm-up, as in Speak Smart and Tale Time.
A theme can run as a short series. Nature x English ran for four sessions in June and July 2023.
Open with something familiar, such as Christmas carols, before the skill, as the December 2025 session at Pather Sathi did.
Clothes and notebook collections are a different kind of drive, and they need their own planning.

faqs.q: How do you run a reading session for kids?
faqs.a: Choose one skill, such as storytelling, public speaking or English grammar, and build the session around a prompt. AquaTerra's student teams usually work with two to five volunteers at a host place, open with something familiar and write the session up afterwards. Since {firstYear}, AquaTerra has written up {count} drives under this heading.

faqs.q: What topics work for a storytelling or English session for children?
faqs.a: Storytelling sessions covered story making, story narration and Halloween tales. Speaking sessions covered public speaking through games and stories. English sessions covered word play and grammar, such as conjunctions and verbs, and financial literacy sessions covered saving and budgeting.

faqs.q: Where does AquaTerra run reading and speaking sessions?
faqs.a: Pather Sathi and Disha Foundation have hosted the most sessions, and Ek Tara, AIM Foundation, Newlight Ngo and School On Wheels have hosted others. In all, the drives on this page ran at {placesCount} places, from schools to shelters.

faqs.q: How many volunteers does a reading session need?
faqs.a: Most sessions had two to five volunteers. Across this topic, {volunteers} volunteer turnouts went into the drives, which counts every time someone came, so one person who came to three sessions is counted three times.

faqs.q: Does AquaTerra teach public speaking to children?
faqs.a: Yes. Public speaking has been a common session type, from Speak Skillfully at Disha Foundation in May 2022, the first session on this page, to PowerSpeak at Pather Sathi in November 2025.

faqs.q: How can I run a reading or speaking session with AquaTerra?
faqs.a: Sign in with Google to join AquaTerra, and wait for your membership to be approved. Members are students aged 14 to 19, and the collaborations page is the place to ask about hosting a session at a school.
